【3】Keep in mind that if normal rotations are present but painful， the problem may still be musculoskeletal in ori-gin (e.g.， SI， early sign of arthritic changes in the hip joint). Full motion is also possible in the early stages of avascular necrosis and sickle cell anemia. 【4】The presence of GI symptoms (e.g.， nausea， vomiting， diarrhea， constipation， abdominal bloating or cramping) or urologic symptoms (e.g.， urinary frequency， nocturia， dysuria， or flank pain) along with hip pain is cause to take a closer look. Palpable reproduction of painful symptoms is generally considered extraarticular.23

【5】Negative radiographs of the hip may not rule out bone lesions. A careful review of risk factors and clinical presenta-tion will guide this decision.24，25

【6】**Groin**

【7】The physical therapist may see a client with an isolated groin problem， especially in the sports or military popula-tions (Case Example 16.3)， but more often， the individual has low back， pelvic， hip， knee， or SI problems with a sec-ondary complaint of groin pain. Possible systemic and/or visceral causes of groin pain are wide ranging， appearing as an isolated symptom or in combination with pelvic， hip， low back， or thigh pain .

【8】Palpating the groin area is usually necessary in making a differential diagnosis. This can be a sensitive issue， and the therapist is advised to have a third person in the examina-tion area. This person should be the same gender as the client. The therapist should explain the examination procedure and obtain the client’s permission.

【9】During examination of the groin， the physical therapist may palpate enlarged lymph nodes， or the client may indicate these nodes to the examiner. Painless， progressive enlarge-ments of lymph nodes or lymph nodes that are aberrant or suspicious for any reason， especially if present in more than one area or in the presence of a past medical history of cancer， are an indication of the need for medical referral.

【10】Changes in lymph nodes without a previous history of cancer continue to represent a yellow or red flag. Tender， movable inguinal lymph nodes may be a sign of food intoler-ance or allergies or an indication that the body is fighting off an infectious process. The therapist should use his or her best clinical judgment in deciding what to do， but should always err on the side of caution. When doubt arises， one should contact the physician and communicate any concerns，obser-vations， or questions.

【11】**_Groin Pain in a 13-Year-Old Skateboarder_**

【12】Referral： A 13-year-old boy presented with a 2-week history of left groin pain. He reported a skateboarding accident as the cause of the symptoms. He was coming down a flight of stairs， hit the last step by mistake， and caught his foot on the stair rail-ing. His leg was forced into wide abduction and external rota-tion. No pop or snap was perceived (heard or felt) at the time of injury.

【13】The client continued skateboarding but experienced increas-ing pain 2 hours later. At that time， he could “hardly walk" and has had trouble walking without limping ever since. He tried getting back to skateboarding but was stopped by sharp pain in the groin. No other symptoms were reported (no saddle anesthesia， no numbness and tingling， no bladder changes， no constitutional symptoms).

【14】Clinical Presentation： An antalgic gait was observed as the boy avoided putting full weight through the hip during the stance phase. Trendelenburg gait or the Trendelenburg test was not positive. He could not do a squat test because of pain. He could not put enough weight on the left leg to try heel walking or toe walking.

【15】Generalized pain occurred along the inner thigh and was described as “tenderness." The child cannot internally rotate the hip past midline. Abduction was limited to 30 degrees with painful empty end feel. During active hip flexion， the hip auto-matically flexes， abducts， and extemally rotates. Pain increases with active assisted or passive hip flexion when one is trying to keep the hip in neutral alignment.

【16】Associated Signs and Symptoms： When asked about symptoms of any kind anywhere else in his body， the boy replied，“No. When offered a list of possible symptoms， these were all negative. He did admit to being slightly constipated because of the pain. Vital signs were all within normal limits.

【59】A 44-year-old male patient came to physical therapy with a 7-year history of right groin pain. X-ray films， a bone scan， and an arthro-gram of the hip were all negative. At the time of initial examina-tion， the client was taking morphine for pain that was described as constant， severe， and sharp and that was rated 8 out of 10on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS； see Chapter 3). Sitting and driving made the symptoms worse， and he was unable to work as a mechanic because prolonged squatting was required. Lying supine relieved the pain.

【60】Physical examination revealed extreme hip medial rotation associated with active hip flexion， abduction， and knee extension； each of these movements reproduced his symptoms. Passive range of motion of the right hip was painful and was limited to 95degrees of flexion and 0 degrees of lateral rotation.

【61】Visual inspection during movement and palpation of the greater trochanter indicated that the proximal femur had medially rotated and moved anteriorly during hip flexion. Through applica-tion of a posteroinferior glide over the proximal femur during hip flexion， groin pain was decreased and motion increased. The cli-ent was able to moderate his symptoms by avoiding hip medial rotation during hip and knee movements.

【72】Chronic groin or inguinal pain in the active athletic， sports， or military groups is often referred to as athletic pub-algia. Athletic pubalgia is sometimes used interchangeably to describe a sports or athletic hernia， which is a tear in the muscles of the inner thigh， lower abdomen， and/or the fas-cia. The term sports hernia may be a bit misleading because experts in this area do not consider this condition the same as a true inguinal or femoral hernia.32

【73】Symptoms associated with athletic pubalgia are often described as deep groin or lower abdominal pain with exer-tion (usually unilateral). There may be a localized sharp burning sensation in the lower abdomen and/or inguinal region. Symptoms are relieved with rest but aggravated by activity， especially sport-related activities that involve cut-ting and pivoting， as well as lateral motions that involve rapid acceleration and deceleration， such as ice hockey， soccer， and rugby.3 As the condition progresses， symptoms may radiate to the adductor region， testes (male)， and labia (female).34，35

【74】Labral tears of the acetabulum can also cause groin pain. There may be a history of trauma but acetabular labral tears can occur without trauma. The clinical pre-sentation can vary and include night pain， activity-related pain， positive Trendelenburg sign， and positive impinge-ment sign (pain reproduced with hip flexion， adduction， and internal rotation： specificity 95.4%， sensitivity 14.8%). In contrast to this， recently， several studies have found a high prevalence of labral pathology in the asymptomatic population.36，37

【75】Femoroacetabular impingement presents as groin pain in young adults. Onset is gradual and progressive with intermit-tent groin pain after prolonged walking， prolonged sitting， or athletic activities that stress the hip. The most reliable hip tests to determine whether a client has femoroacetabular impinge-ment from most reliable to least reliable was the log-roll test(0.99)， the FABER test (0.84)， hip internal rotation causing pain (0.84)， and the anterior impingement test38 (internal h iIpP rotation and adduction while the hip is flexed， 0.76). Referral for a medical orthopedic examination and imaging studies may be warranted.39

【77】Osteitis pubis with inflammation and sclerosis ofthe pubic symphysis can cause both acute and chronic groin pain. Indi-viduals affected most often include competitive sports ath-letes involved in running， leaping， and landing with force， repetitive kicking motions， or training on concrete， uneven， or other hard surfaces. Osteitis pubis can also occur as a result of leg length differences， faulty foot and body mechan-ics， or muscular imbalances and during pregnancy. 【1】6.5 Clinical Manifestations 
-----------------------------------------------

【2】The disease has a range of symptoms, including ulcerative lesions with a bright red granulomatous base that easily bleeds, with hypertrophic or flat borders, which may be ulcerovegetative or with elephantiasis and that may develop necrosis. A varying number of these ulcers can be observed and may sometimes be multiple, and they are chronic and usually not associated with regional lymphadenopathy. Extragential manifestations occur in 6% of cases and systemic dissemination via the blood causing damage to the bone and liver is rare.

【3】6.6 Laboratory Diagnosis
------------------------

【4】Identification of C. granulomatis via Donovan bodies  is most easily carried out using cytological smears and lesion biopsies stained by Wright, Papanicolaou, Giemsa or Leishman technique. These are found inside the cytoplasm of histiocytes and macrophages in the form of encapsulated cocobacilli, which are pleomorphic with rounded edges and become brightly stained with appearance of a safety pin. It is recommended that one swab be taken from the center of the lesion and another from one of the recently developed borders. This procedure is also recommended for biopsies (using the Hematoxylin-Eosin staining technique), which must also contain healthy skin. To the Giemsa staining technique the slide should be air dried, and when using the Wright, Leishman or Papanicolaou techniques the slide should be fixed using alcohol or another cytological fixative agent. A specific kit should be used for analysis of swabs taken from lesions with liquid based cytology. It is true that liquid based cytology can make cellular characteristics easier to observe. However, we do not know of any comparative studies between conventional cytology and liquid based cytology. The culture for this type of bacteria is difficult in terms of its nutritional requirements. Genital lesions over 30 days old, particularly those that have not healed, require histopathological testing. Other diagnostic methods such as PCR and serological screening have still not been standardized or made commercially available.

【14】6.9 Complications
-----------------

【15】Long-lasting lesions can suffer from secondary infections leading to deformations, mutilations and fistulas. In women this may lead to obstructive lymphatic obstructions that can develop into elephantiasis forms. Although rare, extragenital disease can occurr, generally resulting from a primary genital lesions and affecting the bones and other areas, especially in immunosuppressed patients. The development of squamous cell carcinoma in chronic ulcers is well documented, with a high incidence in patients with donovanosis.

【16】6.10 Differential Diagnosis
---------------------------

【17】Syphilis, soft chancre, cutaneous tuberculosis, ulcerative neoplasia, American tegumentary leishmaniasis and other ulcerative and granulomatous cutaneous disease.

【31】**◆There arc three major types of intramedullary spinal cord tumors： gliomas， cpendymomas， and heman-gioblastomas. The first two are malignant and the third is histologically benign.**

【32】**Gliomas account for about half of adult spinal cord tumors， but they account for a higher percentage in children. The peak incidence is in the third and fourth decade. They are most common in the thoracic region， are not usually encapsulated， and usually havc ill-defined borders. They are most common in the thoracic region These tumors tend to extend over the length of a few vertebral bodics but can be much longer.**

【33】**◆上Ependymomas arisc from ependymal cells in the cen-tral spinal canal. Thus， they tend to be central in loca-tion and expand the cord outward. They are soft tumors that usually have a delicate capsule that formns a planc of cleavagc that allows surgical excision without damage to spinal cord tissue. They frequently form cysts. Ependymomas arising in the filum terminale are typically of the myxopapillary type， which are muci-nous and may bleed， causing subarachnoid hemor-. rhage. They may be associated with extremcly high levels of protein in the CSF. Epcndymoma is the most common primary tumor of the lower spinal cord and the filum terminale. Two-thirds of intramedullary tumors at the conus medullaris are ependymomas. Following total removal of the tumor， there is only a small chance of recurrence (about 10%). If the absence of a well-defined capsule prevents total excision， tumor progression， often accompanied by metastases to the CSF or even to distant metastases， is common.**

【34】**Hemangioblastoma is a much less common primary spinal cord tumor (about 3%) than glioma and ependy-moma. About 30% of patients with spinal cord heman-gioblastoma have von Hippcl-Lindau syndrome(VHL). However， <5% of VHL patients are reported to have spinal hemangioblastomas， although the com-mon use of MRI to screen these patients may show that the incidence is， in fact， muich higher.**

They found that these MHI litigants per-formed more poorly on gross relative to fine motor tasks， a pattern opposite that seen in a group of patients with bona fide moderate to|删除1换行|severe closed head injury and neurological evidence of impaired motor function. The geminely impaired subjects showed the typical upper motor neuron lesion pattern of better performance on gross relative to fine motor tasks.**

【2】**Investigations of performance on memory tests show that head trauma malingerers tend to perform more poorly on recognition and/or cued recall relative to free recall than do legitimate brain-injured subjects. Binder， Villanueva， Howieson， and Moore (1993) compared the Auditory Verbal Learning Test (AVLT) performance of a group of MHI litigants identified (on the Portland Digit Recognition Test or PDRT) as having poor motivation， to the performance of a group of normally motivated MHIs， and a group of patients with documented brain dysfunction. Although the three groups were matched on age， education， and AVIT acquisition， the poorly motivated MHIs performed significantly worse on AVLT recognition compared to the other two groups. Only 5% of the brain-injured group obtained AVLT recugnition scores less than 6， where-as 20 of 75 (27%) of the combined MHI group obtained scores less than 6.**

【3】**Millis， Putnam， Adams， and Ricker (1995)， obtained similar findings on the California Verbal Learning Test (CVLT). MHI litigants with low motivation (below chance performance on the Warrington Recognition Memory Test) performed more poorly than non-litigating patients with moderate to severe HI on CVLT Total Trials， Recognition Discriminability， Recognition Hits， and Long-Delay Cued Recall. The best predictors of group membership were Recognition Discriminability and Long Delay Cued Recall. Recognition Discriminability， as a single variable， was the best discriminator between the low motivation MHIs and the bona fide moderate/severe CHI group， with an overall classification rate of 93%.**

【4】**The third category of malingering tasks includes those procedures relying on forced-choice methodology and the normal approxima-tion to the binomial distribution 删除1:<u>(Binder， 1990； Binder & Pankratz，1987； Hiscock & Hiscock， 1989)</u>. In a forced-choice task (e.g.， identi fying whether one has been touched once or twice， identifying which of two 5-digit numbers was presented previously)， it is conceivable that someone with severe brain damage could perform at chance level， a performance that essentially represents zero ability. If subjects perform significantly worse-than-chance， based on the normal approx-imation to the binomial theorem， the assumption can be made that they had to know the correct answer to perform at such an improbably poor level. At extreme levels of probability (.05 or .01)， it can be argued that such an improbable performance is tantamount to con-fession of malingering.**

【5】**Thus， forced-choice methodology provides an opportunity to directly infer intentionally poor performance when someone performs signifi-cantly below chance. In actual clinical experience， many persons whose behavior is suspicious for malingering do not perform at less-than~chance levels on two-alternative forced choice testing. Consequently， several investigators have established objective performance cutoffs rel-ative to performance of a non-litigating bona fide brain damage group， Typically， the cutoff for motivationally abnormal performance is set to mnaximize specificity (i.e.， keep false positives at a minimum). Binder and Willis (1991) defined a PDRT score exceeded by 100% of bona fide brain-injured subjects not in litigation as an absolute (0 percentile) cut-off score. On the PDRT， 16% of litigating MHI subjects performed below this score for PDRT easy items， 26% for hard items， and 30% for total score. Binder and Kelly (1996) revised the cutoff to the bottom 2%of non-litigating brain-injured subjects (98% specificity)， and identified31% of litigating MHIs on the easy PDRT， 47% on the hard PDRT， and43% on the total score.**

【6】**Millis (1992) identified an absolute (0 percentile) score on the Warrington Recognition Memory for Words Test. Fifty percent of litigat-ing MHIs performed below this absolute cutoff. Revising the cutoff identified 70% of MHIs， with only a 10% false positive rate for nonliti-gating severe CHIs.**

【8】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF MHI**

**The preceding sections have provided important information relative to the differential diagnosis of MHl. The outcome data suggesting a low baserate， 5%， of persistent neuropsychological impairment， leading to a low Positive Predictive Value for neuropsychological testing ， and the poor specificity for purported Post-Concussive Symptoms|删除1换行|， highlight the need for careful differential diagnosis in the individual case of MHI with persisting complaints. The review of neuro-logical factors potentially related to persistent dysfunction shows the importance of obtaining early medical records， which may disclose evi-dence of focal neurological abnormalities， prolonged confusion and disorientation， or focal radiological abnormalities. The clinician must base estimates of MHI severity on these acute injury characteristics， rather than on persisting complaints or neuropsychological test abnor-malities 删除1:<u>(Alexander， 1995； Stuss， 1995)</u>.**

【10】**The differential diagnostic consideration of non-trauma factors is extensive. A general discussion was presented in the current chapter， and the interested reader is referred to Binder (1997) for additional review. As Binder (1997) has observed regarding psychiatric differential diagnosis and MHI， “The assessment and differential diagnosis of the kind of head is virtually as broad as the Diagnostic and Statistical _Manual-IV”._**

【11】**Faust， Ziskin，and Hiers (1991) and Larrabee 删除1:<u>(1990，2000)</u> have noted the significant problem of over-diagnosis of neuropsychological deficits in legal settings. The problem of over-diagnosis is the direct result of failure to analyze cases critically and scientifically， Ieading to inadequate differential diagnosis.**

【12】**Faulty logic commonly leads to diagnostic error. The argument： if brain-damaged patients perforni poorly on neuropsychological tests， then any patient who performs poorly on neuropsychological tests must be brain damaged， is the same as the argument： if a horse is an animal with four legs， then any newly encountered animal with four legs is a horse 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 1990； Miller， 1983)</u>. Of course， hippopotami have four legs. and persons can fail neuropsychological tests due to a host of psy-chological and motivational factors.**

【13】**Ignorance of baserates and bias in data analysis are significantly relat ed to over-diagnosis in forensic settings 删除1:<u>(Faust et al.， 1991； Larrabee，2000； Wedding & Faust， 1989)</u>. Wedding and Faust define “hindsight bias” as the tendency to believe， once the outcome of an event is known， that the outcome could have been more easily predicted than is actually the case. For example， a clinician who knows that a patient received a blow to the head in an automobile accident believes he can predict the event and diagnose neuropsychological deficits consistent with closed head injury. Data ignored due to this hindsight bias may include no his-tory of loss of consciousness or post-traumatic annesia and absence of focal neurological sighs at the time ofinitial trauina.**

【14】**“Hindsight bias" is frequently associated with “confirmation bias，”the tendency to favor one's initial hypotheses， and downplay or ignore evidence contradicting these hypotheses. Trope， Gervey， and Liberman(1997) have characterized this bias in judgment as demonstrating evi dence for asymmetric error costs， They also observed that people are Inore likely to terminate hypothesis testing prematurely once receiving evidence supporting their hypothesis.**

【15】**Neuropsychologists engaging in confirmation bias in the evaluation of MHI selectively attend only to evidence that supports their original hypothesis of brain damage. I have described a case 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 2000)</u> diagnosed by another psychologist as having MHI and persisting neu-ropsychological deficits， despite lack of objective independent evidence for blow to the head， loss of consciousness， or post-traumatic amnesia. The other psychologist diagnosed the presence of brain damage on the basis of a WMS-R Attention Concentration Index (AC) of 75. The patient's WMS-R General Memory Index (GM) of I29 was selectively ignored. The psychologist failed to consider the logical inconsistency between evi-dence for impaired attention， at the 5th percentile， and superior memo-ry， at the 97th percentile. The 54-point GM minus AC difference score had a probability of malingering beyond .99 删除1:<u>(Mittenberg et al.，1993)</u>.**

【16】**Wedding and Faust (1989) have provided a variety of strategies for reducing confirmation bias. They recommend that the clinician be familiar with the fitcrature on human judgment . Wedding and Faust recommend that the clinician start with the most valid irform mation， listing alternative diagnostic options and evidence supporting these options， as well as systematically listing disconfirmatory informa-tion. It is as important， if not more so， to list all data that argue against one's hypotheses， as it is to list test findings supporting them 删除1:<u>(Larrabee，2000； Wedding & Faust， 1989)</u>. I recommend framing hypothetical questions such as “What kind of brain damage causes poor perfor-mance on the Category Test， Auditory Verbal Learning Test， and Finger Tapping， with above average performance on Controlled Oral Word Association， Verbal Selective Reminding。 Trail Making B， and the Grooved Pegboard?” 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 2000)</u>.**

**I have also suggested a four-component consistency analysis in neu-ropsychological differential diagnosis 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 1990， 1997，2000)</u>. The data subjected to the consistency analysis include a detailed and|删除1换行|extensive interview， detailed record review， and extensive and redun-dant neuropsychological testing， with multiple measures within each of several neuropsychological domains (e.g.， for attention and informa-tion processing， the Trail Making Test， Stroop， PASAT， and Auditory Consonant Trigrams).**

【18】**The clinical interview is conducted prior to testing. Significant time is spent focusing on the accident， inchuding recall of the events preced-ing and following it. An attempt is made to ascertain recall of facts that can later be validated against medical records (e.g.， time of accident， time discharged from hospital， procedures done in hospital). This allows retrospective analysis of level of consciousness and post-traumatic amnesia， and allows one to estimate initial injury severity. Behavioral observation of the patient during history taking regarding the accident， particularly presence or absence of emotional arousal， can help provide information relative to differential diagnosis of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder. Interviewing regarding subsequent symptom development in relation to time since the accident， health care providers seen， proce-dures undergone， and diagnostic opinions offered to the patient， can later be checked against actual medical records， providing information about the patient's memory， insight， and judgment. Background inter-viewing concerning early development， nuclear family， school experi-ences， work history， marital history， and prior litigation and criminal history is also validated against the appropriate independent records.**

【19】**Following completion ofthe interview， record review， and testing， the consistency analysis is performed. First， test data must be consistent within and between domains. Within domains， a person who performs poorly on Trail Making A should not perform normally on Trail Making B； above average performance on the Grooved Pegboard should not follow impaired performance on Finger Tapping. Between domains， a patient with very poor attention should not perform normally on mem-ory tests； a person with borderline scores on intelligence and problem solving should not have superior memory function.**

【20】**Second， the neuropsychological test score profile should be consis-tent with established patterns for kiown neurobehavioral disorders. Thus， patients whose scores suggest an amnestic disorder should not perform poorly on WAIS-R Digit Span or Arithmetic， patients with scores suggestive of dementia should not perform at above average lev els on complex problein-solving tasks such as the Category Test or WAIS-R Block Design.**

【21】**The third consistency requirement is that level ofneuropsychological test performance should be consistent with severity of original trauma.**

【22】**Dikmen and colleagues (1995) have published one-year neuropsycho-logical outcome data for the full spectrum of head trauma severity， ranging from persons who could follow a doctor's commands within one hour to persons who took greater than one month to follow a doc-tor’s commands. Conseqiently， a patient who was briefly unconscious at the scene of the accident， who recalls transportation to the hospital， entering and leaving the hospital， and who has a Glasgow Coma Scale(GCS) of 15 in the ER， without focal neurological signs and with normal CT scan of the brain， should not perform on neuropsychological testing at levels similar to patients who have sustained two weeks of coma.**

【23】**Lastly， test performance should be compared with other aspects of a patient's behavior. A patient who has good memory in the clinical inter-view， demonstrated by accurate recall of doctors seen and evaluations and treatments， validated by correlation with medical records， should not produce grossly impaired scores on formal memory testing. I saw one MHI patient who performed on memory tesis at a level similar to Alzheimer's patients， yet drove to the examination by himself， and on the second day of examination， noted that a clock had been removed from the wall of the examnining suite.**

【24】**When significant inconsistencies are noted， the clinician must con-sider the possibility of malingering. As noted earlier， a multiple test approach is recommended for assessment of malingering， focusing on both effort on neuropsychological testing and accuracy of the patient's symptomatic report. Above all， everything must make "neuropsycholog-ical sense” 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 1990； Stuss，1995)</u>.**

【25】**CONCLUDING COMMENTS**

【26】**This chapter has considered the differential diagnosis of MHI， defined as an injury characterized by brief LOC， circumscribed PTA， and absence of focal neurological and radiological abnormalities. Data were reviewed demonstrating the small prevalence of persistent neuropsy-chological deficits after MHI. Also considered were the high baserate and consequent poor specificity for the symptomatic complaints thought to characterize post-coneussion syndrome.**

**Discussion of baserates in relation to sensitivity， specificity， PPV，and NPV highlighted the importance of careful differential diagnosis in the individual case of MHI. As a consequence of the low baserate for persis-tent problems following MHI， the clinician is more likely to be correct when not diagnosing than when diagnosing brain impairment. Both|删除1换行|neurological and non-neurological factors were considered relative to persistent neuropsychological test score abnormalities and persisting complaints following MHI. Given the significant baserate for malinger-ing in persons with persistent complaints following MHl， procedures were reviewed for identifying intentionally poor performance and exag-gerated symptom report. A model for scientific differential diagnosis was presented， including consideration of confirmation bias. It is my intent that the material covered in this chapter will assist the clinician in minimizing the occurrence of false positive diagnostic errors in the majority of MHI cases， and maximize the chance of making an accurate diagnosis of the much less common cases of MHI， who truly have persis-tent neurological deficits.**

【6】 The clinical presentation is that of nonbilious vomiting, which gradually progresses in severity over time from low-velocity regurgitation to projectile vomiting. Weight loss, dehydration, and hypochloremic acidosis can occur secondarily. Most patients appear healthy but hungry.

【7】 HPS is characterized by thickening of the circular muscular layer of the pyloric canal, which results in narrowing of the pyloric channel.

【8】 HPS is the most common condition necessitating abdominal surgery in the infant and most common cause of gastric outlet obstruction in the first few weeks of life.

【9】 HPS typically presents in Caucasian boys between the ages of 3 weeks and 8 weeks.

【10】 A palpable thickened pylorus (i.e. so-called olive) in the epigastrium is pathognomonic but is usually detectable only by a trained examiner. When this finding is present in the setting of suspected HPS, no preoperative imaging is necessary. Nonetheless, in most centers a pyloric sonogram will be obtained.

【11】 The treatment is pyloromyotomy. Although spontaneous regression of muscular hypertrophy can occur, nonoperative therapy is difficult to justify given the fact that surgery is quick, safe, and effective.

【12】Radiologic

【13】 Plain film findings include (1) gastric distention, (2) mottled retained gastric contents, (3) indentations in the gastric wall by hyperperistaltic waves (i.e. so-called caterpillar stomach), and (4) diminished air beyond the pylorus.

【14】 Barium study findings include (1) delayed gastric emptying, (2) “string sign” through the pyloric channel, (3) double- or triple-track sign in pyloric channel, (4) “shouldering” in the antrum from muscular hypertrophy, (5) a “beak” sign of oral contrast material at the pyloric entrance, and (6) indentation on the duodenal bulb by the hypertrophied muscularis.

【15】 Sonographic findings include an elongated (i.e. ≥ 15 mm) pyloric channel and increased thickness (i.e. ≥ 3 mm) of the hypoechoic muscle, which are more sensitive findings for diagnosis of HPS than the cross-sectional diameter of the entire pylorus. A “target” or bull’s eye appearance of the pyloric channel is seen on transverse sonographic images.

【16】 Sonographic scanning at an angle tangential to the pylorus can cause a false-positive examination by producing “pseudothickening” of the muscularis. So-called pseudoelongation of the pyloric channel, another potential cause of false-positive examinations, can result from pylorospasm and use of prostaglandins.

【28】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【29】The differential diagnosis for an intramuscular mass in the sternocleidomastoid muscle in an infant with torticollis is very limited.

【30】 Hemangiomas: These are common benign tumors of infancy that are typically dermal or subcutaneous. The classic lesions proliferate in the first few months of life and progressively become uniformly solid with a few associated high-flow vessels. They usually slowly involute over ensuing months or years. The purely intramuscular location and the lack of prominent central and peripheral vessels in the case shown here makes this consideration unlikely.

【31】 Infantile myofibromatosis: Infantile myofibromatosis is a very rare abnormality that affects children during their first two years of life. The lesions may be solitary or multicentric and typically present as a slow growing mass of fibrous tissue. Nearly one-third occur in the head and neck but they can also involve visceral organs (associated with a poorer prognosis). Although this diagnosis can not be absolutely excluded on the basis of the images shown in this case, the rarity of this entity makes it an unlikely diagnosis.

【32】 Sarcoma: Three types of sarcoma could reasonably be considered in the case shown here.

【33】 Rhabdomyosarcoma: Rhabdomyosarcoma can occur at any age and within any muscle. The margins of the lesion may be well-defined or poorly defined.

【34】 Infantile fibrosarcoma: This is a childhood tumor that usually occurs in the legs, but can be found in any muscle. Both rhabdomyosarcoma and infantile fibrosarcoma could produce the imaging findings in the case shown here. However, they are both rare in the newborn period, making them unlikely diagnoses.

【35】 Granulocytic sarcoma (also known as myeloid sarcoma or chloroma): Granulocytic sarcoma can occur in any location and may be solitary or multiple. This rare tumor occurs in infants and children with myeloprolif-erative disorders such as acute or chronic myelogenous leukemia (which would be expected to produce anemia and easy brusiability, absent in the case presented here).

【36】 Fibromatosis colli: This entity, also known as sterno-cleidomastoid pseudotumor of infancy or congenital torticollis, is a benign mass of fibrous tissue that arises within the sternocleidomastoid muscle during the first month of life. Most newborns with torticollis have fibromatosis colli. At sonography, the mass has variable echotexture and causes well-marginated fusiform enlargement of the affected sternocleidomastoid muscle (as is present in the images in the case shown here). This diagnosis is correct.

【37】 Lipoblastoma or lipoblastomatosis: As their names imply, these benign lesions contain fat as well as mysenchymal cells in a myxoid stroma. MR or CT imaging can confirm the presence of fat. Most lesions contain a large amount of fat, but some contain very little fat. The absence of fat makes this an unlikely consideration. Furthermore, lipoblastomastosis is more likely to extend to deeper tissues than in the case shown here.

【38】DIAGNOSIS

【39】Fibromatosis colli

【40】KEY FACTS

【41】Clinical

【42】 Fibromatosis colli is a nontender, benign mass within the sternocleidomastoid muscle of a neonate. The mass consists of fibroblasts, myoblasts, mesenchyme-like cells, and myofibroblasts.

【43】 Fibromatosis colli is a very common neck mass encountered in infancy; it is the most common noninflammatory mass.

【44】 Most often the correct diagnosis is recognized clinically and no imaging is obtained.

【45】 The exact cause of these lesions is not known. The affected infant usually has a history of difficult or traumatic birth, for example, requiring forceps for delivery. Some infants have a history of abnormal positioning of the head in utero.

【46】 Twenty percent of affected neonates have torticollis with the head tilt and chin rotation toward the affected side. In the rare instance when lesions are bilateral, the neck appears short and the chin is tilted upward.

【47】 Treatment is conservative. Physical therapy or no treatment may be used.

【48】 Spontaneous resolution usually occurs by 8 months of age.

【49】 It is uncommon for the abnormality to persist longer than a year or for facial asymmetry to develop. In these cases surgical intervention may be needed.

【50】Radiologic

【51】 Sonography is often used to evaluate an infant with a nontraumatic palpable soft tissue abnormality in the neck.

【52】 At sonography, the mass of fibrous tissue within the sternocleidomastoid muscle caused by fibromatosis colli has variable echotexture, but is relatively homogeneous, and may be well-defined. The enlarged muscle is fusiform.

【53】 Imaging the sternocleidomastoid muscle in both the longitudinal axis and transverse axis is important to confirm that the lesion is completely intramuscular.

【54】 Most cases are unilateral; thus, the uninvolved contralateral sternocleidomastoid muscle can be used for comparison.

【55】 The affected portion of the sternocleidomastoid muscle may be hyperemic.

【57】 CT imaging of fibromatosis colli typically shows an enlarged sternocleidomastoid muscle with normal CT density.

【58】 Associated intramuscular hemorrhage or calcification has been occasionally described on CT and MR imaging.

【71】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【72】 Atelectasis: This diagnosis is a reasonable consideration given the presence of the lung opacity. However, the vessels on the CT examination are not typical of atelectasis. Furthermore, atelectasis would not be expected to persist unchanged on serial radiographs.

【73】 Pulmonary sequestration: This diagnosis is the likeliest consideration (even though a lower lobe location is more typical), given that the opacity persisted. Furthermore, the arterial supply and venous drainage are characteristic of this entity.

【74】 Bronchogenic cyst: This diagnosis is unlikely because a systemic vascular supply would not be expected.

【75】 Arteriovenous malformation (AVM): Pulmonary AVMs frequently have an appearance of multiple, mass-like lesions with prominent feeding arteries, which can be of systemic origin. However, in this case systemic (as opposed to pulmonary) venous drainage is present, which, by definition, is not possible with a pulmonary AVM. In addition, a mass of abnormal lung parenchyma would not be expected in an AVM, making this diagnosis unlikely.

【76】 Pneumonia: The clinical history is not consistent with pneumonia. Furthermore, the prominent vascularity associated with this lesion excludes acute pneumonia.

【77】 Pulmonary neoplasm: Because pulmonary neoplasms are very rare lesions in neonates and because blood supply from the aorta would not be expected in a neoplasm, this diagnosis is very unlikely.

【78】 Chest wall mass: The CT in this case indicates that the mass is within the lung parenchyma as opposed to the chest wall. Furthermore, chest wall masses are rare in neonates (and much less common than pulmonary sequestration). Finally, a chest wall mass would not be expected to have the large vessel vascular pattern that is present in the case illustrated here. This diagnosis is incorrect.

【79】DIAGNOSIS

【80】Pulmonary sequestration (intralobar type)

【81】KEY FACTS

【82】Clinical

【83】 The term sequestration refers to a nonfunctioning pulmonary parenchymal abnormality that lacks normal tracheobronchial communication and has anomalous systemic (rather than pulmonary) arterial supply. Venous drainage may be via systemic or pulmonary veins.

【84】 Seuestration can occur with other congenital lung abnormalities (e.g. bronchogenic cyst, congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation, congenital lobar emphysema \[CLE\]), referred to as a hybrid abnormality.

【85】 Sequestration is part of a continuum of bronchopul-monary foregut malformations (which have variable contributions of anomalies of lung, airway, and vascu-lature). Traditionally, a distinction is made between an intralobar (i.e. no separate pleura) and an extralobar (i.e. having a separate pleural investment) type of sequestration.

【86】 Modes of presentation generally differ according to the age at the time of diagnosis.

【87】 In the prenatal period, the diagnosis is based on the finding of an echogenic chest mass at sonography or fetal MRI.

【88】 The clinical presentation in the neonatal period can be respiratory distress. However, infants can be asymp-tomic.

【89】 In a child (and occasionally an adult), the clinical presentation is that of recurrent pulmonary infections, with the sequestration often initially being misdiag-nosed as pneumonia. The sequestration is most often an “incidental” finding unrelated to clinical findings, suggesting lower respiratory infection.

【90】 More than half of sequestrations present in childhood. Most extralobar sequestrations are discovered within the first year of life.

【91】 Sequestration can occasionally present in an infant or small child as a murmur with congestive heart failure due to the arteriovenous shunting.

【92】 The intralobar type is more common and can be congenital or acquired. Most are lower lobe in location, with two-thirds located on the left side. Drainage is usually via the pulmonary veins.

【93】 The extralobar type also usually occurs in the lower lobe and is on the left side in 90% of cases. This type may also be subdiaphragmatic. Drainage is typically through systemic veins. Fifty percent of cases have associated anomalies e.g. heart disease, diaphragmatic hernias, gastrointestinal, and other pulmonary abnormalities.

【94】 Treatment for pulmonary sequestrations is surgical excision, which may be deferred for a period of 6 to 12 months, if the neonate is asymptomatic.

【95】Radiologic

【96】 The sequestered lung can receive air flow through collateral sources. Therefore, if recurrent infections have not occurred, the radiographic appearance can be normal.

【97】 The diagnosis should be considered when persistent or recurrent lower lobe opacity is found.

【98】 Catheter angiography has been replaced by other, noninvasive imaging studies to determine vascular supply. Multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) angiogra-phy is the preferred method of diagnosis but MRI can also be especially useful.

【99】 Sonography with color Doppler can be used to document arterial supply if a good acoustic window is present to facilitate imaging; however, usually cross-sectional imaging is performed prior to complete evaluation.

【1】**Assessment**

【2】Assessment of many of the obsessive-compulsive and related disorders (OCRDs) located in this chapter is challenging due to the diverse nature of the underly-ing disorders as well as their frequent comorbidity with each other as well as other mental disorders. For example， according to the DSM-5， nearly 75% of individuals with hoarding disorder frequently have a comorbid major depres-sive disorder or an anxiety disorder and 20% co-occurring OCD 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>. Furthermore， research has lead to the acknowledgment of common symptom dimensions (e.g.， cleaning/contamination， symmetry/counting) that accompany these disorders as well as the variety of insight in afflicted individu-als (good to absent insight/delusional beliefs).

【17】Emergency Considerations Isolation， stigma， and functional impairment are all too common in individuals suffering from the mental disorders contained in this chapter. When treating individuals with an obsessive-compulsive re-lated disorder (OCRD)， which often overlap with other diagnoses， it is im-portant to address suicide risk. Although the research on OCD and suicide is limited and at times contradictory， assessment of the suicide ideation and intent may be warranted. One study of suicide and OCD by Kamath， Reddy， and Kandavel (2007) reported a 10-27% lifetime suicide attempt rate as well as high rates of suicidal ideation. Similarly， Fawzy and Hashim (2011) concluded that suicidal ideation in OCD is more prevalent than was earlier believed， and it is strongly interrelated with sociodemographic factors. Yet another study found that although suicide behavior in OCD is not highly common， it poses a greater risk in individuals who were diagnosed with OCD， unmarried， with comorbid depression and symmetry/ordering obsessions and compulsions 删除1:<u>(Alonso et al.，2010)</u>. These results are consistent with the findings on other OCRDs. Studies on BDD show it is often associated with high rates of suicidalideation， attempts， and completion at 45 times the rate of the general population 删除1:<u>(Phillips， 2007)</u>.

【18】In the National Guidelines Clearinghouse’s “Practice guideline for the treat-ment of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder” published by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality， enhancing the safety of the patient with OCD is paramount to practice as these individuals have a higher suicide attempt rate than the general population. They also point out that individuals with OCD rarely perpetrate violent behavior. Assessing the risk of self-harm and suicide from intrusive thoughts and compulsions (i.e.， Do they have an active plan and intent?) can be challenging particularly if accompanied by co-occurring disorders and poor insight. Care must be taken when evaluating individuals for suicide risk as aggressive/sexual themes can often be misinterpreted as indicating risk.

【19】Cultural Considerations

【20】Although the prevalence and clinical features of OCD is relatively equal world-wide 删除1:<u>(Staley & Ward， 1995)</u> research shows that ethnic minorities (African Americans， Asians， and Hispanic/Latinos) in the United States are less likely to re-ceive treatment for OCD and are underrepresented in OCD clinical trials 删除1:<u>(Chow， Jaffee， & Snowden， 2003； Himle et al.， 2008； Williams， Powers， Yun， & Foa，2010； Williams， Turkheimer， Schmidt，& Oltmanns， 2005)</u>. The same was found for ethnic minority children. Without treatment， ethnic minorities are more likely to suffer lifelong disability and impairment despite effective treatments.

An explanation for this access to treatment disparity between the majority and minority populations may be a function of cultural， racial， and ethnic dif-ferences. Cultural factors can influence the mental health of racial/ethnic minori-ties， especially in terms of help-seeking behaviors. Williams，Domanico，Marques， Leblanc， and Turkheimer (2012) found that major treatment barriers for African Americans included fear and distrust about the therapist and therapeutic process as well as the stigma and judgment associated with a diagnosis of a mental dis-order. For many Asian and Hispanic Americans， cultural barriers include stigma and shame as well as language and acculturation barriers and traditional family structure that relies on the family to handle problems without outside assis-tance 删除1:<u>(APA， 2007a， b； Kramer， Kwong， Lee， & Chung， 2002)</u>. Also， considering|删除1换行|the vast cultural heterogeneity of African/Black， Hispanic/Latino， and Asian pop-ulations the lack of culturally appropriate services may also be a deterrent.

【22】Another possibility for this disparity may be measurement bias and the possibility that differences in responses to questions about mental health are a function of cultural/racial/ethnic differences. Research suggests that current self-report instruments for OCD may be inadequate for assessing diverse racial/ethnic groups. Replicating earlier studies， it was demonstrated that African Americans score significantly higher on levels of cleaning symptoms using contamination scales of OCD than European Americans (even higher than those reporting a diagnosis of OCD). Often， this symptom expression did not meet the diagnostic criteria for OCD， as it did not always result in reports of anxiety or distress删除1:<u>(Williams et al.， 2005)</u>. Research on this self-reporting difference suggests that it should not be attributed to greater psychopathology in African Americans and may be the result of correlations with nonpathological attitudes. In effect， a greater concern with cleanliness may be a cultural norm for African Americans删除1:<u>(Williams & Turkheimer， 2007)</u>. In general， the most common obsessions are fears of contamination and cleaning/washing compulsions. Implications for prac-tice include a focus on subjective distress and time spent on compulsions rather than specific behaviors 删除1:<u>(Williams， Turkheimer， Magee， & Guterbock， 2008)</u>.

【23】Although the core clinical features of OCRDs appear independent of cultural variations， cultural differences can be found in the presentation and expression of illness symptoms/behaviors. However， information is limited on how cul-ture， race， and ethnicity can impact symptom expression in these disorders. For example， studies of highly religious cultures (Christian， Jewish， Muslim) from around the world (Middle East， Asia， and the United States) have demonstrated that religion and culture can affect OCD symptom expression manifesting in religious obsessions and compulsions including cleaning rituals and compulsive praying. In religious cultures， religion can provide an excellent method of con-cealment for ritualizing. However， it is important to note that religion does not increase the prevalence of OCD in the very religious； rather it is often the outlet of choice for symptom expression.

【24】Although the prevalence of BDD and clinical features appears to be similar in many different cultures around the world (approximately 1-2%) and has been documented for over a century， research on cultural， racial， and ethnic differences is very limited. Some data suggest that cultural factors (i.e.，appear-ance preferences) may influence symptom presentation in BDD. For instance， Phillips (2004) found eyelid concerns and the fear of displeasing others by being unattractive a common symptom in Japan but rare in Western countries. As with all disorders， clinicians need to be mindful of the possible overlap of symptoms with culture-bound syndromes. For instance， taijin kyofusho and koro， both culture-related syndromes occurring in Japan and southeast Asia have similarities to BDD but differ in duration， fears， and response. As noted in the DSM-5 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>， a disorder known as shubo-kyofu translated as the phobia of a deformed body， may bear a close resemblance to BDD in terms of symptomatology.

【27】Gender

【28】Gender differences have been reported among the obsessive-compulsive and re-lated disorders. Studies of OCD show that males are more likely to be single， have earlier onset， and a more chronic course with greater impairment. Fur-ther， gender-related social roles may affect the content of obsessions and com-pulsions. Males tend to report more religious/sexual and aggressive symptoms and females more contamination/cleaning symptoms 删除1:<u>(de Mathis et al， 2011)</u>. Research on gender differences in BDD is limited and prevalence ratios by gender vary with data showing more similarities than differences. Males were more likely to be older， single/living alone， have a comorbid substance use disorder with excessive body concerns around thinning hair/balding， genitals， and muscularity. Females tended to have a greater number of body concerns， have comorbid eating disorder with greater distress over excess body hair， and weight/body composition. These concerns carried out in BDD behaviors with males reporting more weight lifting behaviors and women more camouflaging techniques and mirror checking behaviors. Of interest， Phillips， Mena061200rd， andFay (2006) reported inconsistent findings when comparing scores by gender on three BDD severity measures. After controlling for the presence of eating disorders the higher scores found for females on one scale was eliminated. 【244】**Case Study Analysis**

【245】After history and examination were obtained， the patient continued to have tremors of his hands and involuntary movement of his neck. He also became manic and had to seek psy-chiatric care for imp

【0】arated from one another by zones of orthokeratosis， slight spongiosis and epider-mal hyperplasia， a sparse superficial perivascular predominantly lympho-cytic infiltrate， and dilated capillaries and venules in the upper part of the dermis.

【1】That eruptive psoriasis is a rapidly evolving process can be inferred from the presence of neutrophils in the epidermis and dermis， mitotic fig-ures above the epidermal basal layer， and extravasated erythrocytes in the papillary dermis and， at times， the epidermis. Edema of the papillary der-mis and sspongiosis are other reflections of the dynamic nature of guttate psoriasis.

【2】Guttate parapsoriasis is much more indolent than guttate psoriasis. In sequential biopsy specimens， very slight spongiosis is evident in sections of fully devcloped lesions that are topped by distinctive elongated mounds of parakeratosis within which droplets of plasma often reside. The tad of plasma is testimony to spongiosis having been present within the epidermis， even if no spongiosis is detectable presently in a particular section.

【3】Clinically， guttate parapsoriasis consists of non-pruritic， drop-sized， pink to tan papules that are covered by fine， wafer-like scales. Lesions may be widespread， but they favor the buttocks， flanks， and thighs， just as do other flat and slightly elevated manifestations of mycosis fungoides. They tend to persist and are notoriously refractory to treatment. In our view， guttate parapsoriasis and digitate dermatosis are merely different names for different clinical manifestations of the same pathologic process， the lesions of digitate dermatosis simply being elongated in the shape of fingers pressed against the skin. The distribution of the lesions of the guttate and the digi-tate types is the same. Guttate parapsoriasis， as we use the term， is not synonymous with parapsoriasis lichenoides， i.e.， it is unrelated to Mucha-Habermann disease. Guttate parapsoriasis/digitate dermatosis must be dif-ferentiated histopathologically from pityriasis rosea and its look-alike ery-thema annulare centrifugum， and that is accomplished by finding denser superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes， more prominent spongi-osis， and shorter mounds of parakcratosis in pityriasis rosea and erythema annulare centrifugum.

Small papular lesions of guttate psoriasis may erupt as an effect of a streptococcal infection in children and young adults. In this setting， the papules often regress without therapy. At other times， however， the guttate|删除1换行|lesions may coalesce to form plaques or become so widespread that an erythroderma results. Papules may remain guttate for a protracted period. Eruptive lesions of psoriasis may become pustular as a consequence of ac-celeration of pathophysiologic mechanisms inherent in the psoriatic pro-cess. When the inflammatory process accelerates in lichen planus and sys-temic lupus erythematosus， bullous expressions of those discases result.**

【5】**For many years， we (and many others) thought that guttate parapsori-asis and its variant digitate dermatosis (grouped together under small plaque parapsoriasis”) were inflammatory diseases unrelated to mycosis fungoides. We now are impressed by the fact that some patients with indu-bitable patches and plaques of mycosis fungoides also bear lesions typical of either guttate parapsoriasis or digitate dermatosis， or both. We also have seen lesions， thought clinically to be guttate parapsoriasis or digitate derma-tosis， that showed subtle histopathologic signs of mycosis fungoides， e.g.， a slightly spongiotic focus peppered by lymphocytes， some lymphocytes ar-ranged as solitary units in the epidermal basal layer， and， at times， hints of wiry bundles of collagen arrayed haphazardly in concert with patchy lym-phocytes infiltrates in the papillary dermis. These observations fortify our view that guttate parapsoriasis/digitate dermatosis， and other manifesta-tions of small plaque parapsoriasis， just like those of large plaque parapsori-asis， represents a flat manifestation of mycosis fungoides.**

【6】**Superfluous synonymy associated with the term “parapsoriasis”has created confusion for students of skin diseases for more than a century. The term initially was used for lesions that clinically bore some resemblance to true psoriasis. 【55】**_A_ s their names denote， herpes simplex is caused by a herpes virus and cowpox (vaccinia) by a pox virus. Both are DNA viruses that induce skin lesions which share many histopathologic features， e.g.， intraepidermal vesicles surrounded by ballooned keratinocytes，reticu-lar alteration， and signs of necrosis of what originally were steel-gray nuclei. Viral inclusions are harbored in keratinocytes of both discases. Intraepider-mal vesicles may rupture， and， as a consequence， subepidermal blisters come into being. Neutrophils may be present within the epidermis and may form pustules there. Epithelial structures of adnexa tend to be involved by changes similar to those in the epidermis. 【56】**These two viral diseases can be distinguished when unique changes caused by herpesvirus are recognized within epithelial cells. The homogene-ous steel-gray appearance of nuclei is framed by condensation of nuclear chromatin. In vaccinia， although nuclei aiso may have a steel-gray color， coarse chromatin is distributed throughout them. Eosinophilic and am-phophilic inclusions are present within nuclei of keratinocytes infected by herpesvirus， whereas inclusions in vaccinia arepresent within the cyto-plasm. Herpesvirus induces acantholysis of epithelial cells， but vaccinia does not. In infections of vaccinia， but not in those of herpesvirus， cytoplasm retracts from nuclei.**

**Clinically， lesions of herpes simplex have been likened to dew drops poised on a petal of a rose， i.e.， small， tense， often umbilicated vesicles grouped upon a pink-red base. The word “herpetiform” now is employed for blistering processes， apart from those caused by herpesvirus， in which there is a tendency for vesicles to form quickly and in clusters， as they do in dermatitis herpetiformis and herpes gestationis， neither of which has been shown to be a viral disease. Because of the many similarities t veen them， authentic pemphigus vulgaris and the pemphigus vulgaris-like vari-ant of Grover’s disease may be indistinguishable from one another in a particular section， especially if a lesion is sampled by a small biopsy.

Pemphigus vulgaris involves the epidermis across a broad front and extends in dramatic fashion far down epithelial structures of adnexa. The changes of Grover’s disease occur in tiny discrete foci， and when adnexal involvement occurs， it usually is subtle， superficial， and unassociated with prominent signs of acantholysis.

【89】Pemphigus vulgaris is predominantly a discase of middle-aged persons， but it may begin in childhood. 【50】Rubella virus belongs to the Togaviridae family. In children， it is responsible for a mild disease. This is characterized by the classic nonconfluent maculopap-ular rash， which appears on the face first and then disseminates to the trunk and limbs. In the adult， the disease may be more severe， with significant arthral-gia， cough， conjunctivitis， and headache.

【51】The risk of transmission is up to 80% if the infection is acquired in the first trimester， with 85% of the infected fetuses developing severe infection and/or malforma-tions. Multiple defects are more common for infections acquired in the first eight weeks of pregnancy. After12 weeks， the risk of vertical transmission decreases rapidly， to re-increase after 30 weeks of gestation (60%).

【52】Diagnosis of maternal infection. If the pregnant woman has a rash consistent with rubella infection， the follow-ing should be checked： (1) if a previous rubella anti-body test is available (which occurs in most cases， due to widespread maternal screening)， and (2) when the onset of maternal symptoms occurred. If these data are known， a simple blood sample allows definition of the situation. In fact， positive IgM and positive or nega-tive IgG (if both were negative on the initial pregnancy rubella test) indicate current infection. A second blood sample taken after seven to ten days will show increase in the IgG levels and confirm the IgM positivity. In the absence of a former rubella test， the IgG avidity should be assessed： if the avidity is hig1ity 15h， the infection is olderthan six months； and if it is low， then it has occurred in the past three months.

【53】If the pregnant woman has had contact with a rubella-like illness， and if she is susceptible to rubella from her initial pregnancy testing， then IgG and IgM levels should be assessed on her serum for a few weeks， to check whether she may show seroconversion.

【54】**A significant increase in the Ig G levels in a woman with already positive IgG who has had contact with a rubella-like illness stands in favor of reinfection.**

【55】**Diagnosis of fetal infection. There are two issues that make prenatal diagnosis and US in rubella infection different from those for CMV and Parvovirus B19：**

【56】(1) an initial pregnancy rubeo-test is available in the overwhelming majority of cases； and (2) most cases are referred because of maternal rubella or contact with a rubella-like illness. Therefore， in this case both prenatal diagnosis and US are carried out in a fetus known to be at risk for the disease.

【57】Prenatal diagnosis is carried out by checking the presence of the viral DNA by PCR on the amniotic fluid more than 7-8 weeks after maternal infection and anyway after the 21st week of gestation. Reverse tran-scription PCR (RT-PCR) on multiple samples should be used. However， the patient should be aware that false negative results may occur， although on exceedingly rare occasions. Main indications to prenatal diagno-sis are represented by the following 通用删除6(英):<u>\[27\]</u>： (1) equivocal IgM results in the first trimester， which do not allow one to rule out maternal infection； (2) when， more fre-quently， maternal rubella infection is confirmed by the lab to have occurred in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy； and (3) when rubella reinfection is confirmed to have occurred in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy.

【58】Ultrasound. The sonographic assessment of a fetus with rubella infection may disclose two different pat-terns， according to the time of infection. If this has occurred in the first trimester， then major congenital anomalies may be present； if， on the other hand， infec-tion has occurred later， and also in some of the ear-lier infections， then signs of congenital infection but not malformations may be present. Malformations associated with rubella infection in the first 12 weeks of gestation (especially the first eight weeks) include cerebral， eye， cardiac， and skeletal anomalies. In par-ticular， cerebral abnormalities include microcephaly， leukoencephalopathy， and basal ganglia calcifications. Neuronal loss may lead to severe mental retardation. In addition， central or neurosensory hearing loss is also frequent in congenital rubella syndrome.

【13】LARGECELLCALCIFYINGSERTOLICELLTUMORLarge cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumor is a rare tumor of Sertoli cell origin that can result in hyperestrogenemia and gynecomastia通用删除6(英):<u>\[72\]</u>.Lesscommonly， testosterone production may be observed通用删除6(英):<u>\[73\]</u>. When this group of tumors was first described， it was noted that they werecommonly associated with bilaterality，mul-tifocality， endocrine disorders， familial occurrence， and cardiac myxomas \[741. Later it was determined that these associations were due to their occurrence as a part of Peutz-Jeghers syn-drome and Carney complex.

【14】While large cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumor is characteris-tic of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and Carney complex 通用删除6(英):<u>\[75\]</u>，it may also be seen in patients who are not affected by either of these disorders 通用删除6(英):<u>\[76\]</u>. Those cases notassociated with one of these syndromes usually present between 13 and 34 yrof age， are more likely to be unilateral and unifocal， and can be treated with orchiectomy alone as the prognosis is generally favorable 通用删除6(英):<u>\[76-78\]</u>， unless features associated with malignantbehavior are iden-tified 通用删除6(英):<u>\[79\]</u>. One case of large cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumor was associated with unilateral renal agenesis and inferior vena cava duplication， but this may be a chance association 通用删除6(英):<u>\[77\]</u>.

【15】Grossly the tumors average approx 2 cm at presentation and are well circumseribed， solid， and yellow to gray-tan 通用删除6(英):<u>\[72，76\]</u>. The tumor cells are arranged in nests or cords surrounded by basementmembrane material and myxoid to fibrous stroma with an inflammatory infiltrate that includes neutrophils 通用删除6(英):<u>\[76\]</u>.The tumor cells are large with lightly to densely eosinophilic cyto-plasm 通用删除6(英):<u>\[72\]</u>. Centrally located small spherical or larger amor-phous calcifications are typical but not always present 通用删除6(英):<u>\[76\]</u>. An interesting finding in some cases is the presence of u-l-antitrypsin-containing cytoplasmic hyaline globules in Sertoli cells in the uninvolved seminiferous tubules 通用删除6(英):<u>\[76\]</u>.

Inhibin is expressed by Sertoli cells and may be useful as a serum tumor marker \[811.

【17】These tumors generally behave in a benign fashion 通用删除6(英):<u>\[78\]</u>； however， occasional cases are malignant 通用删除6(英):<u>\[79，82，83\]</u>. Malignant

【19】GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR Granulosa cell tumors very rarely occur in the testis. These tumors morphologically resem-ble the more common ovarian granulosa cell tumor and the granulosa cells of the normal ovarian follicle. The presence of this tumor in the testis has been explained by the capacity of primitive sex-cord cells to differentiate into tissue found in either type of gonad 通用删除6(英):<u>\[84\]</u>. As in the ovary， two types of granu-losa cell tumor are recognized： adult type and juvenile type. The adult type has been reported in men from 16 to 76 yrof age通用删除6(英):<u>\[85\]</u>. Adult-type granulosa cell tumors may be associated with hyperestrogenemia and resulting gynecomastia and loss of libido 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>. However， these tumors more commonly lack endo-crine manifestations \[851.

【20】The adult-type granulosa cell tumors are grossly well cir-cumscribed and usually yellow. Solid， cystic， microfollicular， and trabecular patterns may be seen on microscopic examina-tion. Call-Exner bodies， rosettelike structures with a round， smooth-bordered central space， are seen in about half of the cases . The tumor cells have scant cytoplasm and oval nuclei. A key cytologic finding is the presence of longitudinal nuclear grooves 通用删除6(英):<u>\[85\]</u>. The tumor cells are immunohistochem-ically positive for vimentin and negative for epithelial membrane antigen 通用删除6(英):<u>\[85\]</u>. Focal cytokeratin positivity has been reported通用删除6(英):<u>\[86\]</u>， but not in all studies 通用删除6(英):<u>\[85，87\]</u>. Membranous O13 (CD99， Ewing sarcoma antibody) positivity has also been noted 通用删除6(英):<u>\[86\]</u>. Ultrastructural findings include occasional desmosomes，cyto-plasmic glycogen， rough endoplasmic reticulum， and folded nuclear membranes， similar to ovarian granulosa cell tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[88\]</u>.

【19】### 3 Agnosias

【20】Marlene Behrmann and Maxim D. Hammer

【21】Neurologic Differential Diagnosis , ed. Alan B. Ettinger and Deborah M. Weisbrot. Published by Cambridge University Press. © Cambridge University Press 2014.

【22】#### Introduction

【23】Agnosia (a-gnosis, or loss of knowledge) refers to a class of neuropsychological impairments in which the affected individual is unable to recognize an object successfully. This recognition failure can occur in the visual, auditory, or tactile modality, and arises despite preserved sensory information in that modality. In other words, the primary sensory modalities are preserved but there is impairment of higher-order representations of objects in the affected domain. The recognition impairment is neither attributable to an anomia or to a semantic deficit (or lack of knowledge about objects in general) because patients can successfully identify the same object presented in a different sensory modality. The preserved long-term representation of objects can also be revealed as, for example, patients with visual agnosia may be able to visualize a particular object in their “mind's eye” but, presented with the same object, may fail to identify it.

【24】##### Visual agnosias

【25】Because visual agnosia is the best-studied instance of the agnosias, we focus more specifically on this impairment here. Patients with visual agnosia may have fully, or at least relatively, preserved visual acuity 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 \]</u> and sensory vision (e.g. contrast sensitivity or brightness discrimination) and fall into one of at least three subtypes. Apperceptive agnosia corresponds to the breakdown at the stage of visual processing at which the elementary features of the stimulus are processed and a structural description of the input is derived – a relatively early stage of the visual recognition system . Not surprisingly, a person with apperceptive agnosia fails to produce a coherent copy of a target stimulus and fails to match a visual target against a set of choice objects. In contrast, a person with associative agnosia cannot use the well-specified perceptual representation to access the stored knowledge of the object's functions and associations – for example, such an individual is able to copy and match a target object while still unable to identify the object (this disorder is often described as “perception stripped of meaning”). Whether perception is entirely normal in associative agnosia remains somewhat controversial. Finally, integrative agnosia, recognized more recently than the other subtypes and likely lying intermediate between the two other types, refers to the impairment in grouping disparate elements of the display into a coherent whole, with a piecemeal approach to perception 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 , 3 \]</u>. Such individuals may be able to copy and match a target object but this is done in a slow, segmental, and laborious fashion, perhaps feature-by-feature.

【30】It is thought that these subtypes of agnosia reflect a spectrum of impairments in the different stages in object recognition and localization of lesion 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 \]</u>. Thus, apperceptive agnosia has been associated with more posterior diffuse lesions resulting from mercury or lead poisoning or from carbon monoxide inhalation whereas the higher-order forms of agnosia are associated with more focal lesions situated more anteriorly in the visual system. Figure 3.1 depicts the lesion of a patient, SM, who sustained damage to the right occipitotemporal lobe and who suffers from integrative agnosia. SM can match and copy objects albeit in a slavish fashion. Like other agnosic individuals, SM's failure to recognize objects occurs under a whole range of conditions and is independent of whether the stimulus is presented as a real three-dimensional object, black-and-white line drawing, or as a photograph 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u>. Dramatically, SM's perceptual failures occur despite normal or near-normal elementary visual function, along with normal semantic and memory functioning. SM, like other agnosic individuals, also has intact alertness, intelligence, and language, thus setting aside questions about whether agnosia is simply a manifestation of reduced elementary visual function and intelligence.

【32】Although agnosias are usually acquired in adulthood as a consequence of a stroke, tumor, trauma (as in SM's case), or other form of brain damage, there are a few cases of agnosia reported in individuals who have sustained a brain lesion early in life, a disorder referred to as “developmental agnosia.” Agnosia may also be evident in individuals who are apparently impaired at object recognition from birth but in the absence of any obvious neurologic concomitant 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 , 7 \]</u> . Finally, agnosia can occur in the context of a progressive deterioration of perceptual skills, as in the case of visually selective progressive posterior cortical atrophy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 8 \]</u>.

【33】Visual agnosia can be general, affecting the recognition of all visual stimuli or, in the higher-order form of the disorder, it can be more specific 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>: for example, there are agnosias that are relatively selective for objects, or for body parts, or for colors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Topographic agnosia is another variant in which patients have difficulties with scene perception and different subtypes exist including landmark agnosia (the failure to recognize buildings and scenes), problems in cognitive map formation , or heading disorientation (a failure to discern the relationship between objects in the environment). The lesion in such cases may implicate the fusiform and lingual gyri, extending to the parahippocampal gyrus.

【34】Prosopagnosia , in which there is failure to recognize familiar faces or even discriminate between novel faces, is typically associated with normal voice and face recognition. In many instances, these patients can describe the face in detail, including the age and gender of the person, but still be unable to say whose face it is. The ability to extract information about emotional expression is preserved in some cases but not in others. The prosopagnosia deficit is typically perceptual in nature, rather than arising from a memory (although there are prosopamnesic cases for whom this is the core of the deficit) or semantic deficit, nor from a failure to label the face (an anomia). The acquired form of the disorder usually results from a lesion to the right fusiform gyrus although some more anterior lesions could produce the same outcome (also, for left versus right lesions, see 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 \]</u>). The developmental or congenital variant of prosopagnosia has received considerable recent attention, with growing recognition that there is a familial component and that the incidence may be as high as 2% in the population 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 12 \]</u>. Prosopagnosia, especially the congenital form, must be differentially diagnosed from autism spectrum disorder and other social disorders.

【35】Patients with left posterior lesions, usually to the so-called visual word form area of the fusiform gyrus, evince a deficit in word recognition with intact writing abilities (and hence the failure to read what she herself has written), termed pure alexia or agnosic alexia. The deficit may extend beyond the ability to recognize text per se, impairing the recognition of other alphanumeric stimuli, too, and even affecting object recognition 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 \]</u>. These patients have normal language function and may be able to spell words out loud.

【36】The agnosias catalogued above all implicate problems in visual shape perception but there have also been occasional reports of patients who have preserved shape processing but impaired perception of material properties, such as texture 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>.
